name: Activity Guidance & Exercise Safety Guardrails
purpose: Use genotype as a weak context modifier for training questions while keeping symptoms, medical history, progression, and professional clearance ahead of genetic optimization.
principles: Do not use raw DNA to clear a person for high-intensity, contact, endurance, heat, altitude, or maximal-load activity.
Start with the user's current ability, goals, symptoms, medications, sleep, nutrition, and training history; increase load gradually.
If phenotype, clinical history, or a professional's restriction conflicts with a genetic suggestion, the phenotype or clinical direction wins.
Treat training recommendations as adjustable experiments with symptom and recovery feedback, never as genetic destiny.
stop_and_escalate: Chest pain, pressure, or unusual tightness during or after activity
Fainting, near-fainting, confusion, or unexplained severe dizziness
Unusual or severe shortness of breath, blue lips, or low oxygen
Fast or irregular heartbeat with symptoms
Dark urine, severe weakness, or severe muscle pain after exercise
Sudden neurologic symptoms, severe allergic symptoms, or heat-illness symptoms

domains.context: ACTN3, recovery, mitochondrial, creatine, and myopathy-related markers
favor: training-log review of soreness, sleep, performance, and hydration
sports-medicine review when exercise intolerance or recurrent injury is present
avoid: maximal testing or rapid training-load increases when severe fatigue, cramps, dark urine, or exercise intolerance is present
claiming a power/endurance genotype determines performance
confirm_with: sports-medicine evaluation when red flags occur

domains.context: Collagen, ligament, tendon, hypermobility, and bone-density context
favor: technique-first progressive resistance and low-impact conditioning when tolerated
physical-therapy or sports-medicine movement assessment when instability or recurrent injury is present
avoid: using a common SNP to clear aggressive stretching, contact sport, heavy lifting, or return-to-play
rapid load changes when pain, instability, fracture history, or neurologic symptoms are present
confirm_with: DXA or imaging when clinically indicated

domains.context: Blood-pressure, lipid, thrombosis, arrhythmia, and vascular context
favor: gradual aerobic and resistance progression matched to current symptoms and clinical status
blood-pressure, lipid, and recovery monitoring when those markers are relevant
avoid: high-intensity or maximal-effort clearance from genotype alone
ignoring exertional chest pain, fainting, palpitations, or unusual breathlessness
confirm_with: ECG or exercise testing when a clinician indicates
cardiology review for exertional red flags

domains.context: Asthma, airway, lung-function, oxygenation, and sleep-apnea context
favor: symptom- and environment-aware conditioning with appropriate warm-up
clinician-guided asthma or airway plan when symptoms limit exercise
avoid: using genotype to rule out exercise-induced bronchoconstriction or sleep-related breathing problems
pushing through wheeze, severe breathlessness, low oxygen, or faintness
confirm_with: pulmonary review for persistent or severe symptoms

domains.context: Cycle timing, contraception, menopause, pregnancy/postpartum, and hormone-therapy context
favor: symptom- and cycle-aware adjustment of training load, sleep, hydration, and recovery
prospective symptom and training tracking across cycles when cyclic changes are reported
avoid: assuming a hormone level, ovulation status, pregnancy status, or exercise restriction from DNA or chromosome-call context
changing contraception or hormone medication because of a training response or genotype
confirm_with: cycle or life-stage context supplied by the user
clinician review when bleeding, pelvic pain, pregnancy, or postpartum red flags are present
